content: ‘I’ve set the agenda’ says Hanson on migration Pauline Hanson says the two major parties are following her footsteps on migration policy because “they realise that I’m right in what I’m saying”. She tells News24 she’s set the agenda on the issue – ahead of shadow housing minister Andrew Bragg today announcing that the Coalition will set the net overseas migration number to 180,000 per year over the forward estimates. At the moment, the permanent migration level is set to 185,000 while the net overseas migration in the last financial year was estimated to be 295,000. Net overseas migration is the total number of people coming into the country minus those going out – which can make it harder to predict and control than the permanent migration level. Hanson says: They [Labor] brought in one and a half million people in their term of being in government, and they intend to bring in another one million people over the next four years. We can’t cope with this. The people are saying it, and that’s why now I’ve set the agenda. Both the political parties, Labour and Liberal, are pulling back their numbers because they realise that I’m right in what I’m saying. I’m bringing in 130,000 a year, net migration in the country. While she says her policy is 130,000 NOM, her website states that One Nation “cap visas at 130,000 per year to ease pressure on housing, wages, and infrastructure” which sounds little different. Going back to Ted O’Brien and James Paterson demanding an AFP investigation into melon-gate, it’s interesting to note that the Coalition has taken it upon itself to express “deep regret” to Japan over Anthony Albanese’s comments – despite the very diplomatic cable at the centre of their calls for a police investigation, showing Japan’s government did not want to make a major issue out of the podcast comments. O’Brien and Paterson, no less than the shadow ministers for foreign affairs and defence, today have demanded the AFP investigate the apparent leaking of a diplomatic cable to The Australian newspaper, suggesting police check whether the prime minister’s office was involved. O’Brien said he met the Japanese ambassador last night, and “expressed my deep regret of the prime minister’s actions”. He said he had “no authority to speak on behalf of the government or prime minister, but if I did have such authority, I would have apologised … but I did make that expression to the ambassador”. Of course, the diplomatic cable at the centre of the Coalition’s concerns today indicates Japan wasn’t that offended in the first place. As reported by The Australian, the cable claimed there had been “sensationalised reporting in the Australian media”, that Tokyo believed there was no “ill intention” in Albanese’s actions, and they would take “no action” in hopes that it would “allow the Australian media to move on”. We asked O’Brien about this, but he rejected there was any discrepancy in those two issues. “I won’t be commenting on how Tokyo interprets this entire saga,” O’Brien said at a press conference. He then stared down the barrel of the camera to speak directly to “anyone who is watching, whether it be the Japanese Australian community here locally, or whether it be anybody visiting from Japan”, saying “Australia takes our relationship with your country very seriously.” Taylor tries to suspend standing orders over melon-gate The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, has turned up the heat in the lower house this morning, immediately moving to suspend standing orders to get the prime minister to apologise over melon-gate. Because the government has the numbers, it won’t go anywhere, but it’s a move to keep the whole debacle ticking along. Taylor says an apology would show Albanese, “who is known for his hubris, can be capable of humility”. This prime minister has stuffed up. He has made an egregious error. He had earlier posted on social media and I quote, No matter who you support in politics, it is completely unacceptable to demean, objectify, belittle, or offend women. Oh, really? Nice words. If this is the standard, the prime minister sets for others, it’s the standard he should also hold himself to. I call on the prime minister to pick up the phone and apologise to the Japanese prime minister. Australia has joined the US and dozens of other nations including the UK, France, Germany and the Philippines, in calling on all relevant countries to provide advanced notice of ballistic missile launches. Why does this matter? The joint statement of 40 nations follows a series of launches in the Pacific, including a ballistic missile test by North Korea, and a nuclear-capable missile test by China last month. Only a few Pacific nations were signatory to the statement, including Palau and the Marshall Islands. The statement says countries should provide 24 hours notice before the launch of intercontinental ballistic missiles, submarine-launched ballistic missiles, and space launch vehicles. Conducting nuclear-capable ballistic missile tests without sufficient advance notice and detail is dangerous and disrupts the peace and security of relevant nations in proximity to these tests. It increases the risk of miscalculation, undermines global stability and security, and is incompatible with the responsibilities that come with possessing long-range missile capabilities. Victorian parliament has voted to abolish group voting tickets (GVTs) to elect its upper house. The state was the only remaining jurisdiction with the system, in which voters can only choose one party above the line on the ballot paper, with their preferences then allocated by the party if it’s knocked out during counting. GVTs have been criticised by experts including Antony Green because they allowed backroom deals between parties to flourish, enabling some candidates to get elected with only a minuscule number of primary votes. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚政治直播：蒂姆·威尔逊质疑住房能效标准，称“有些人称之为穿套头衫”
chineseContent: 汉森在移民问题上表示，“我已经制定了议程”波琳·汉森表示，两大政党正在追随她在移民政策上的脚步，因为“他们意识到我所说的是对的”。她告诉 News24，她已经就这个问题制定了议程——今天，影子住房部长安德鲁·布拉格 (Andrew Bragg) 宣布，联盟党将把海外净移民人数设定为每年 18 万，高于预期。目前，永久移民人数为185,000人，而上一财年的海外净移民人数估计为295,000人。净海外移民是进入该国的总人数减去出境人数 — — 这可能比永久移民水平更难预测和控制。汉森说：他们（工党）在政府任期内吸纳了一百五十万人，他们打算在未来四年内吸纳另外一百万人。我们无法应对这个问题。人们都这么说，这就是我现在制定议程的原因。工党和自由党这两个政党都在减少选票，因为他们意识到我所说的是对的。我每年为这个国家带来 13 万净移民。虽然她说她的政策是 130,000 NOM，但她的网站称 One Nation“将签证上限限制在每年 130,000 个，以缓解住房、工资和基础设施的压力”，这听起来没什么不同。回到特德·奥布莱恩和詹姆斯·帕特森要求法新社对瓜门事件进行调查的问题上，有趣的是，联盟已自行对安东尼·阿尔巴内斯的言论向日本表示“深切遗憾”——尽管他们呼吁警方调查的核心是外交电报，表明日本政府不想做出任何改变。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
